question: During the COVID-19 pandemic, the media shed light on the ‘shadow pandemic’ of domestic violence. The proposed directive on combating violence against women and domestic violence signifies a crucial step in tackling this concerning issue. To effectively address domestic violence, a comprehensive system must be established, encompassing funding, detection, protection and prevention. Priority should be given to safeguarding vulnerable groups, with stringent controls implemented in the family environment. 1.
Ηow does the Commission intend to develop an efficient system for detecting and protecting against domestic violence, alongside supporting preventive measures and implementing robust controls?

Does the Commission plan to fund and establish a helpline or support lifeline service for victims that will record and evaluate complaints, provide legal, psychological and law enforcement protection, while also identifying incidents of child crime and conducting preventive checks in the family environment?

Ηow does the Commission aim to guarantee that the detection of domestic violence through social media or the authorities will not expose the victim, while ensuring that they immediately receive the necessary protection and that high social standards are in place?
answer: On 24 April and 7 May 2024 respectively, the European Parliament and the Council officially adopted the directive on combating violence against women and domestic violence (1), the first-ever EU law in this area. The directive provides obligations for the detection of instances of violence (e.g. trainings to enable relevant authorities to identify cases of violence); the protection of victims (e.g.
individual assessment of the victim protection needs immediately after the first contact with competent authorities and ensuing adoption of protection measures); specialist support (including, e.g.

, specialised support for victims of sexual violence); prevention (including specific measures to prevent rape and promote the central role of consent in sexual relationships) and the obligation to establish an official body responsible for monitoring policies and measures to prevent and combat violence against women and domestic violence.

The directive also requires special attention and support for victims who face a heightened risk of violence due to their experiencing intersectional discrimination (e.g. women with dependant residence status; lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans or intersex persons, etc.)

The directive requires that a state-wide telephone helpline be available, free of charge, 24/7, to provide information and advice to victims, and encourages Member States to ensure that such services are reachable through the harmonised number at Union level: 116 016.

The safety of the victim is ensured through various provisions that ensure the victim’s anonymity (helpline) or private life (in criminal proceedings), while ensuring at the same time that they receive appropriate protection, support and access to justice.
Directive (EU) 2024/1385 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 May 2024 on combating violence against women and domestic violence, OJ L 24.5.2024, p. 1.
